learning_outcomes.text: Identify the basic elements of a thermal power plant, their function, and operating conditions.
Know the processes and parameters that define them, and evaluate their performance.
Know the technology in each of the cases.
Analyze the possibilities of energy saving and environmental impact of each of the studied machines and power plants.
Propose the thermodynamic design of a power plant.
Identify and discriminate different types of reciprocating engines, and equipment (turbomachinery, boilers, combustion chambers), and subsystems of thermal power plants.
Know the scope of application of different types of thermal engines.
Evaluate environmental repercussions of using one or another technology for power generation.
The ability to solve problems.
The ability to search, communicate and discriminate relevant information to characterize a power generation facility.
The ability to work in a team and distribute workload to tackle complex problems.
A critical attitude regarding how to identify and evaluate the performance and operation of the elementary equipment that constitutes an installation.
A collaborative attitude that allows obtaining necessary information and knowledge from other agents to perform complex tasks.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
Adequate knowledge of their engineering branch, including some cutting-edge knowledge in their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility and standards of engineering practice.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem solving within their area of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions, and to apply environmental and sustainability technologies.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
Applied knowledge of thermal engineering.

syllabus_topics: Brayton and Rankine cycles for power production, improved cycles.

Simple, inter-cooled, reheated, regenerative Brayton cycles, complex and closed cycles. Study of different types of combustion chambers. Velocity triangle in compressor and turbine, as well as operational limitations in gas turbines due to thermal resistance of blades. Blade cooling systems.

Simple, reheat, regeneration (steam extractions and drains) Rankine cycles. Complete cycles. Study of boiler parts and different types of condensation. Analysis of Feed Water Heater operation in regenerative power generation cycles. Drain Cooling Approach and Terminal Temperature Difference parameters.
Study of combined cycle operation. Analysis of 1-pressure level heat recovery steam generators. Description of two and three-pressure level heat recovery steam generators.

Fundamentals of concentrated solar power plants: Global energy production. CO2 emissions. Paris Climate Conference. European energy status. Concentrated solar energy: Solar energy, effect of absorption temperature, heat transfer fluid, energy storage system, concentration technologies, parabolic trough, linear fresnel, solar tower, Stirling dish.

Fundamentals of nuclear energy (Position of nuclear energy in the world and in Spain, fuel, uranium enrichment, reactor types (PWR, BWR), thermodynamic cycle, reaction control, cooling. Recent advances in nuclear technology.

Cogeneration: Overview of cogeneration systems. Thermodynamics and efficiency indicators in cogeneration plants. Cogeneration plants with steam turbine. Cogeneration plants with gas turbine. Cogeneration plants with reciprocating internal combustion engines. Other cogeneration and trigeneration technologies.

Internal combustion engines: Description and analysis of internal combustion thermodynamic cycles. Spark ignition engines (SI) and compression ignition engines (CI). Engine architecture. Description of the operation of the main parts of an internal combustion engine: cylinder-piston assembly, timing (camshaft, crankshaft), valve timing, cooling. Efficiencies in ICE, specific, indicated, mechanical.
teaching_methods: Joint discussion and correction of solutions
assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 60% from the ordinary exam and 40% from continuous assessment. Continuous assessment comprises 10% from laboratory practices and 30% from Partial 1. A minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required on the ordinary exam. Resit arrangements are governed by the general university regulations.
